references.text: Abimelech and Phicol came to Abraham and said that God was with him in all he did, and asked for a covenant – an almost identical situation that repeats itself with Isaac in Gen 26:28.
God's promise to be with Isaac is the background for Abimelech being able to acknowledge that the Lord was with Isaac in v.28.
Jacob and Laban made a covenant, reflecting the same pattern of formalizing relationships through oaths and covenants, as Abimelech proposed in Gen 26:28.
Joseph's master saw that the Lord was with Joseph and let everything succeed for him – the same pattern where surroundings recognize God's presence with a person, as in Gen 26:28.
Jonathan made a covenant with David and his house, a parallel to the covenant theme in Gen 26:28 where parties seek to secure a peaceful relationship through a formal agreement.
All the tribes of Israel came to David and recognized his calling – an example of others recognizing God's election and presence with a person and seeking alliance with him.
Recognition of God's presence among God's people leads outsiders to seek to join them.
